findings.title: Ribbon-fan pin resolves the router via nonexistent node id 8 and discards the lookup's ok — passes by coincidence of the (0,false) fallback slot
findings.evidence:
rim := puck_rim_world(&v, 4)
		rs, _ := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 8)
		nw := node_world(&s.topology, rs, 26.0) — wire_setup spawns only ids 0-5; core/topology.odin:93 `return 0, false` on miss; slot 0 happens to be the router
findings.detail: 5-lens agreement. node_slot(8) fails (ids 0..5 only); ok discarded; rs=0 is coincidentally the router slot so the apex assertion measures the right node by accident. rim also uses port_capacity 4 while the router is router_mid (8 ports). Any fixture reorder silently weakens the pin.
findings.recommended_fix: rs, ok := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 0) with testing.expect(t, ok); rim := puck_rim_world(&v, 8) to match the router_mid under test.

findings.title: Shipped spec artifact still carries pre-verdict 'full deliberate T2 re-bless' language, contradicting verdict C (no re-bless) recorded in the same PR
findings.evidence:
- `goldens/*` -- full deliberate T2 re-bless (cause-documented); T1 + replay byte-identical
- [x] `goldens` -- VERDICT C: no re-bless needed (shipped flags off -> byte-identical T2) -- full deliberate T2 re-bless; T1/log.bin byte-identical
- Given the re-bless, when the harness runs, then T1 manifests + replay logs are byte-identical to pre-7.5
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. Lines 61/74/84/113 describe a full T2 re-bless that per verdict C never happened and must never happen. The canon fold (stories-v2.md + decision-log) is correct; only this artifact contradicts itself.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the Code Map goldens line, the goldens task, and the 'Given the re-bless' acceptance criterion to the verdict-C wording (no re-bless; harness run on committed goldens is the proof).

findings.title: Bend-cap exit ships a polyline that may still cross/sprite-clip — the spec's 'still crosses after the bend cap → STRAIGHT' half is unimplemented
findings.detail: When the loop exits because bends == WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_BENDS, no final scan_obstacles runs: a path still violating after the 3rd bend ships bent. Only the length-ratio half of the spec's degradation contract exists. Flags-off today, so no shipped-pixel impact.
findings.recommended_fix: After the bend loop, run one final scan_obstacles; if found, wire_path_straight(&p, apex_a, apex_b) before the ratio check.

findings.title: Degradation fallback is never exercised: the only fixture produces a straight path, so the ratio/bend-cap trip is asserted vacuously
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. No fixture forces WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_LEN_RATIO fallback, WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_BENDS exhaustion, WIRE_STUB_TILES skip-cross, or edge/sprite detours. Hard requirement #4 (graceful degradation) has no boundary coverage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add fixtures that force a crossing whose detour exceeds 1.5× straight (assert n==2 fallback), force the bend cap, and a stub-terminal crossing (assert skip_cross); assert edge/sprite detours land.

findings.title: The 6 wire-path pins (incl. the load-bearing cost-immunity pin) are run by no ci-local gate — suite stays 10/10 even if they rot
findings.evidence: "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|odin test core" — the only odin-test entry in the GATES array; .github/workflows/ci.yml:70 likewise runs only `odin test core`; `odin build app` never compiles _test.odin files
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. Pins are green today (verified: 6/6) and gate 4's T1/replay independently pins cost immunity end-to-end, so this is a durability gap, not a live defect. But the suite the guards call ground truth would stay green if the pins rotted.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an 11th gate (or extend gate 2) running `odin test app/render`, mirrored in .github/workflows/ci.yml per the step-for-step parity rule.

findings.title: Flags-ON render variants have zero automated coverage; the wire-preview gate tool is exercised by no CI gate (preview-check is the unrelated R2a assist check)
findings.evidence: "Assist preview cross-check (R2a preview == sim routing)|tools/harness.sh preview-check" — harness/assist_check.odin:476 'assist preview-check: N scenario(s) green (preview == sim routing)'
findings.detail: The routed/anchor draw branches (draw_bundles, draw_packets, draw_selection, draw_crisis_outlines, draw_glow_edge) execute only when a human runs `harness wire-preview` by hand; T2 goldens all run flags-off. Variant draw helpers can break silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a smoke gate that runs `harness wire-preview` into a temp dir and asserts exit 0 + non-empty PNGs (or hash-pin one routed frame); keep it cheap since the variants ship OFF.

findings.title: Frozen Intent promises anchors 'aligned to the incident directions' but the code allocates a rotated regular template independent of each pipe's actual direction
findings.evidence: spec: 'Anchor allocation: at a router, n incident pipes get n anchors evenly spread around the puck, aligned to the incident directions (deterministic, snapped to the pinned CIRCLE16 table...)' vs code: return (base + int(f32(rank) * 16.0 / f32(n) + 0.5)) % 16 — base is the MEAN incident direction
findings.detail: Anchors sit at base + rank*16/n on the 16-gon; base is the mean of incident directions. For symmetric layouts (the ✕/＋) the read is exact; for asymmetric routers anchors do not align to the pipes' actual directions, contradicting the frozen spec text. Presentation-only, flags-off.
findings.recommended_fix: Either snap each pipe's anchor to its own direction16 index (resolving collisions deterministically) or amend the spec wording to 'even template anchored at the mean direction'.

findings.title: Pixel-level 'rendered twice → identical SHA-256' determinism claim has no in-tree artifact — true and reproducible (Perkins re-ran it: 14/14 frames byte-identical) but not durable
findings.evidence: 'a pixel-level determinism check (two renders of the same frame, byte-identical hashes)' — no hash code exists in harness/wire_preview.odin; path-level determinism IS pinned (test_path_determinism)
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. Perkins independently ran harness wire-preview twice → all 14 PNGs SHA-256 identical, so the claim is TRUE and reproducible from the shipped code. The gap is durability: the check is a manual one-off, not a committed verb or test.
findings.recommended_fix: Either add a harness self-test that renders a routed frame twice and compares SHA-256, or reword the PR body to call the pixel check a one-off manual verification.

findings.title: draw_glow_edge recomputes wire_path_compute per edge instead of threading the frame's shared paths slice like every other consumer
findings.evidence:
path: Wire_Path
		if v.route_wires {
			band_w := band_world(v, bundles.bundle_tier[bi], int(bundles.bundle_count[bi]))
			path = wire_path_compute(v, topo, bundles, bi, band_w) — vs draw_world's 'computed once per frame ONLY when a wire aesthetic is active' + paths[:] threading to draw_bundles/draw_packets/draw_selection/draw_crisis_outlines
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. Four consumers thread draw_world's one-per-frame paths; draw_glow_edge re-derives the path locally (duplicating band_w in both branches). Output identical (pure function) but the plumbing is inconsistent and recomputes per DAG edge when flags flip on.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass the paths slice into draw_glow_edge like the other consumers and index paths[bi]; hoist the shared band_w above the branch.

findings.title: Lane-stripe composite block duplicated between the legacy and variant branches of draw_bundles
findings.evidence: for i in 0..<3 { lane_cols[i] = rl.Color{ u8(f32(col.r)*0.72 + f32(lane_cols[i].r)*0.28), ... } } — identical block in both the flags-off and 7.5-variant branches
findings.detail: 2-lens agreement. The 7.1 bird's-eye hint composite (0.72/0.28 toward the tier color) now exists twice. Math is deterministic and pixel-identical from either site, so the duplication is not required for golden byte-identity; a future lane-read change must touch both copies.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared helper (lane_stripe_colors(v, col) -> [3]rl.Color) used by both branches; legacy stays byte-identical since the computation is unchanged.

findings.title: bundle_end_anchors/end_apex discard pp.node_slot's ok — silent fallback to node slot 0
findings.detail: A failed node_slot lookup silently yields slot 0, so anchors/apexes compute from the wrong node's geometry. No OOB (slot 0 valid whenever the topology is non-empty), but it contradicts the file's own defensive-bound helpers and the errors-are-values rule.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture ok from pp.node_slot; on failure emit no anchors (return empty) or fall back to the straight node-center path explicitly.

findings.title: Pin suite only exercises the primitive-fallback radii; the shipped sprite-target branches of puck_rim_world/building_foot_world are untested
findings.evidence: test_view: v.sprites.ok = false — vs puck_rim_world: if v.sprites.ok { return sprite_puck_target(v, port_capacity) * 0.5 / max(v.scale, 0.0001) } — harness/goldens.odin render_setup uses the sprite path (sprites_load)
findings.detail: Every anchor/radius pin runs with sprites disabled, so the sprite-target radius math (the configuration the game and harness actually render with) has no coverage; only the primitive fallback constants are pinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one pin that sets v.sprites.ok=true (stub targets) and asserts puck_rim_world/building_foot_world match the sprite_*_target-derived radii.

findings.title: Dead locals in scan_obstacles: unused `segs` and discarded intersection point `X`
findings.evidence: segs := max(1, path.n - 1) — never referenced again; X, t, ok := seg_cross(a, b, c, d) — X unused (the edge scan at line 503 uses the `_` idiom: _, t, ok := seg_cross(...))
findings.detail: Two dead bindings in the new module; compiles clean but inconsistent with the file's own `_` discard idiom and the project's lean-code conventions.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the segs line and change X, t, ok := seg_cross(...) to _, t, ok := seg_cross(...).

findings.title: bundle_end_anchors discards its `end` parameter (`_ = end`) and then immediately branches on it
findings.evidence: bundle_end_anchors :: proc(... end: u32, ...) { _ = end ... if end == 0 { ... } else { ... }
findings.detail: The `_ = end` discard is a leftover no-op directly contradicted by the `if end == 0` three lines later. Harmless but signals an unfinished edit; same smell as `_ = b` in test_cost_stays_on_logical_length.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the `_ = end` line (and the redundant `_ = b` in the test); the parameters are genuinely used.

findings.title: Anchor.idx is written at every append site but never read anywhere in the diff
findings.evidence: Anchor :: struct { pos: rl.Vector2, idx: int, tier: u16 } — writes: append(&out, Anchor{pos=..., idx=direction16(...), tier=...}) — consumers read only anc.pos and anc.tier
findings.detail: The fan-stub loop and end_apex read anc.pos/anc.tier only; idx is dead weight carried through every anchor. Either consume it (debug/verification) or drop it.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove idx from Anchor, or use it in a test/assertion verifying anchors land on the intended 16-gon steps.

findings.title: wire_preview.odin header documents 6 emitted PNGs; the code emits 14
findings.evidence: // Emits: // <outdir>/juice_routed.png <outdir>/juice_straight.png // <outdir>/estate_routed.png <outdir>/estate_straight.png // <outdir>/closeup_juice_routed.png (2.4x zoom) // <outdir>/closeup_estate_routed.png — code also emits closeup_*_straight, fan_estate_*, *_anchors frames (Perkins ran it: 14 PNGs)
findings.detail: The r2 additions (anchors candidates, straight close-ups, 5x fan shots) were appended without updating the Emits list, so the file's own documentation describes half its output.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the header Emits block to list all 14 frames including the straight close-ups, the 5x fan shots, and the r2 anchors candidates.

findings.title: band_world restates band_width's formula, against the file's own ONE-definition convention
findings.evidence: band_world :: proc(...) { return (tier_pipe_width(v, tier) + f32(max(0, count-1)) * BUNDLE_EXTRA_WIDTH) * 2.2 } — vs view.odin band_width: same formula * v.scale, with 'ONE definition — a restated copy drifts' comment
findings.detail: band_world is band_width ÷ scale restated (same 2.2 factor, same BUNDLE_EXTRA_WIDTH term) — exactly the drift pattern band_width's comment prohibits. A future band-width tune silently desyncs detour clearances from drawn widths.
findings.recommended_fix: Define band_world as band_width(v, tier, count) / max(v.scale, 0.0001) so the 7.1 band formula stays single-source.

findings.title: draw_bundles requires a paths argument with no default while draw_packets/draw_selection/draw_crisis_outlines all default paths to nil
findings.evidence: draw_bundles :: proc(v, topo, bundles, flow, crisis, paths: []Wire_Path) — vs draw_packets(..., paths: []Wire_Path = nil), draw_selection(..., paths: []Wire_Path = nil), draw_crisis_outlines(..., paths: []Wire_Path = nil)
findings.detail: Four consumers of the same paths slice, three with `= nil` defaults and one without — inconsistent call contract for no evident reason.
findings.recommended_fix: Give draw_bundles the same `paths: []Wire_Path = nil` default as its sibling consumers.

findings.title: The shipped flags-OFF state (route_wires/wire_anchors) is asserted by no test
findings.evidence:
app.view.route_wires = false
	app.view.wire_anchors = false — harness/goldens.odin:57-58 sets the same; no test references either flag
findings.detail: Both flags are pinned OFF only by explicit init assignments; T2 goldens pin the harness render (flags false) but nothing guards the app binary's flag state — deleting the two app/main.odin lines changes the shipped look with zero test signal.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a tiny pin asserting a freshly-initialized app/harness View has both flags false, or a lint grep gate on the two assignment lines.
